note: Yet another shape: a top-level 'vehicles' array where highlights is a real array but 'features' is a SEMICOLON-DELIMITED string, and price is in lakhs rather than rupees.

vehicles.description: The default small-car answer in India: frugal, easy to park and cheap to keep running. Refinement and highway stability are ordinary.
The safety pick of the compact SUV segment, with a heavy, planted feel. Software and fit-and-finish lag the Korean rivals.
The segment benchmark for comfort and features, and the easiest of these to sell on later. Not remotely engaging to drive.
Enormous power and space for the money with genuine seven-seat usability. Long waiting periods and variable quality control.
A quiet, hybrid seven-seater that returns small-car fuel economy. It is expensive and the boot shrinks with the third row up.
A city EV with a real 300km usable range and near-zero running cost. Charging infrastructure remains the limiting factor outside metros.
One of the longer-range electric SUVs under 26 lakh, with strong straight-line pace. Resale value for EVs is still unproven.
The most refined petrol engine in its class and a genuinely large boot. Ground clearance is a real concern on bad roads.

vehicles.features: panoramic sunroof;360 camera;ventilated seats;heads up display
vehicles.description: Nearly 28 kmpl from a self-charging hybrid makes this the cheapest SUV to run. The hybrid battery eats into boot space and it feels slow when pushed.

vehicles.features: adas level 2;panoramic sunroof;bose audio;dual 10 inch screens
vehicles.description: The most enjoyable engine in the mid-size SUV class paired with a genuinely premium interior. Firm ride at low speeds.

vehicles.features: heads up display;360 camera;6 airbags;wireless carplay
vehicles.description: The most spacious premium hatchback with a features list normally seen a segment above. Light doors and thin sheet metal feel cheap.
The best-finished cabin among premium hatchbacks. The naturally aspirated engine is unexciting and it is pricey for the segment.
A big, planted highway cruiser with real presence and a torquey diesel. Fuel economy and rear visibility are both poor.
The enthusiast's sedan: quick, stable at speed and safe. Service costs and dealer coverage are the long-standing worry.
A body-on-frame SUV that holds value better than anything else here and will cross anything. Thirsty, unwieldy in cities, and very expensive.

vehicles.features: heads up display;360 camera;6 airbags;wireless carplay
vehicles.description: A turbo-petrol crossover that is quick in the city and still returns 20 kmpl. Rear seat space is tight for three adults.
Feels the most solid of the mid-size sedans and the DSG is genuinely quick. Infotainment software is dated and service is expensive.
A real off-roader you can drive daily, and it turns heads everywhere. Four seats, a tiny boot and poor rear-seat comfort.
The most affordable route to seven seats and it rides beautifully over broken roads. Only three NCAP stars and a sparse features list.
Long range and a very safe battery chemistry, with strong acceleration. Interior design is polarising and the dealer network is small.
About the least expensive automatic on sale and easy in traffic. The two-star crash rating is a serious mark against it.
The fastest mainstream sedan here and loaded with driver aids. The styling is divisive and low-speed ride is firm.
Rides and handles better than any Japanese or Korean rival at the price. Reliability reports and service costs are the risk.

vehicles.features: cng kit;6 airbags;cruise control;rear ac vents
vehicles.description: The lowest running cost per kilometre of any seven-seater on sale. The CNG tank fills the boot and performance is weak when loaded.
A coupe-SUV EV with a genuinely usable 400km real-world range and a big boot. Rear headroom suffers from the sloping roof.
Boxy, upright and easy to place on the road, with Honda's reliability record. The CVT gearbox drones and there is no turbo option.
